project.name: benebot
project.description: BeneBot is a synthetic-data medical-bill guide that separates historical EOB adjudication from current Stedi eligibility, supports bilingual Deepgram voice plus deterministic text fallback, and persists confirmed Medplum workflow artifacts.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Authenticated POST endpoint that loads the session-scoped historical bill from Medplum, allows an explicitly configured fixture fallback, refuses unreconciled math, and returns deterministic bilingual narration.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Verifies the signed session, resolves historical bill context, enforces the math-reconciliation gate, shapes the public tool result, and attaches a code-generated spoken summary.

nodes.name: benebot-panel.tsx
nodes.summary: Primary bilingual voice-and-text experience that connects Deepgram Agent hooks to the five BeneBot server tools, preserves deterministic billing narration, handles fallback routing, and displays confirmed benefit and follow-up results.
nodes.languageNotes: A large client component isolates Deepgram provider configuration at the boundary while validating every tool payload with Zod before updating UI state.

nodes.name: BenefitValue
nodes.summary: Renders a labeled optional monetary benefit, preserving unknown values instead of fabricating an amount.

nodes.name: CurrentBenefitsCard
nodes.summary: Displays a separately timestamped current-benefits result with coverage, deductible, out-of-pocket, copay, coinsurance, source, and warning details.

nodes.name: ResourceOptions
nodes.summary: Renders support-resource cards while preserving each resource's source disclosure and verification status.

nodes.name: FollowupStatus
nodes.summary: Shows success only for a server-confirmed billing-review Task and otherwise presents an explicit failure state.

nodes.name: VoicePanelContent
nodes.summary: Coordinates Deepgram session state, interruption handling, deterministic text fallback, tool sequences, benefits and resource displays, confirmed follow-up creation, and concise summary persistence.

nodes.name: BeneBotPanel
nodes.summary: Creates the language-specific Deepgram provider, obtains a temporary server-issued token, dispatches validated function calls, and converts deterministic tool output into constrained agent responses.

nodes.name: tool-activity.tsx
nodes.summary: Accessible status list showing the five most recent BeneBot tool operations as running, confirmed, or failed.

nodes.name: ToolActivity
nodes.summary: Renders recent tool activity with live-region semantics and distinct visual states without overstating success.

nodes.name: transcript.tsx
nodes.summary: Conversation renderer that combines Deepgram entries with text-fallback messages and shows a privacy-oriented empty state.

nodes.name: Transcript
nodes.summary: Displays voice and fallback conversation entries with role-aware styling, auto-scroll, and a no-raw-audio empty-state message.

nodes.name: historical-narration.ts
nodes.summary: Pure formatter for a complete English and Spanish historical-claim explanation using only already-normalized values and an explicit historical-versus-current limitation.

nodes.name: formatDate
nodes.summary: Formats date-only and timestamp values in the selected language while preserving invalid input unchanged.

nodes.name: buildHistoricalRequiredSpokenSummary
nodes.summary: Builds complete bilingual narration from reconciled bill fields and emits a number-free safety response when reconciliation fails.

nodes.name: contracts.ts
nodes.summary: Shared TypeScript contracts for the closed five-tool surface, historical bill data, current benefits, support resources, follow-up Tasks, concise Communications, and activity events.
nodes.languageNotes: Discriminated literal unions encode the bounded tool surface and make success, fallback, verification, and unknown states explicit at compile time.

nodes.name: concept-guidance.ts
nodes.summary: Code-owned bilingual healthcare-billing dictionary for six adjudicated concepts, including preferred terms, safe analogies, analogy boundaries, and prohibited phrasings.

nodes.name: createApprovedConceptGuidance
nodes.summary: Compiles the approved generic concept dictionary into selected-language prompt guidance without importing patient-specific examples.

nodes.name: config.ts
nodes.summary: Builds Spanish- or English-specific Deepgram Agent configuration with Flux multilingual recognition, billing keyterms, matching Aura voices, a low-temperature reasoning model, temporary-token auth, and bounded reconnect behavior.

nodes.name: createDeepgramAgentConfig
nodes.summary: Returns a language-matched Deepgram listen-think-speak configuration using a server token factory, the five tool definitions, and the safety prompt.

nodes.name: prerequisites.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the use conditions, server-confirmed prerequisites, permitted outputs, and fail-closed behavior for each of BeneBot's five tools.

nodes.name: createToolPrerequisitePrompt
nodes.summary: Serializes the closed tool prerequisite table into compact prompt rules for the voice agent.

nodes.name: prompt.ts
nodes.summary: Safety-focused system prompt separating historical EOB adjudication from current Stedi eligibility, requiring deterministic tool narration, fixed session language, explicit confirmation, and server-verified external actions.

nodes.name: createBeneBotAgentPrompt
nodes.summary: Composes the base BeneBot policy with closed tool prerequisites, selected-language concept guidance, and a fixed language-session directive.

nodes.name: text-fallback.ts
nodes.summary: Deterministic bilingual text-intent router that preserves the same historical/current separation, clarification, hardship-resource, confirmation, and summary-saving flow when voice is unavailable.

nodes.name: inferTextLanguage
nodes.summary: Chooses English or Spanish from explicit language requests and a bounded Spanish vocabulary, otherwise retaining the current language.

nodes.name: categorizeBillingIssue
nodes.summary: Maps patient text to one narrow billing-review issue category and a concise language-matched summary for confirmation.

nodes.name: routeTextFallbackIntent
nodes.summary: Routes fallback text through confirmation, clarification, bill, current-benefits, hardship-resource, language-switch, and summary-saving states, including an ordered history-then-current tool sequence.

nodes.name: summaryLanguage
nodes.summary: Records whether a concise conversation summary is English, Spanish, or mixed without storing a transcript.

nodes.name: tools.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the exact five Deepgram tools, validates their arguments with Zod, maps them to authenticated server routes, and reports sanitized running, success, or failure activity.

nodes.name: isToolName
nodes.summary: Type guard that accepts only names in the closed BeneBot tool-route map.

nodes.name: dispatchBeneBotTool
nodes.summary: Validates a tool call, posts it to the corresponding server route with the signed session, emits activity updates, and returns only sanitized JSON success or failure output.

nodes.name: provider.ts
nodes.summary: Validates and searches the local synthetic support-resource fixture, ranks practice-provided results first, caps output at three, localizes content, and preserves disclosure metadata.

nodes.name: toSupportResource
nodes.summary: Projects a validated fixture record into the public language-specific support-resource contract while preserving provenance and disclosure fields.

nodes.name: LocalJsonSupportResourceProvider
nodes.summary: Local fallback provider that filters synthetic resources by need and language, prioritizes stronger sources, limits results, and returns visibly labeled JSON-backed matches.

nodes.name: resource-provider.test.ts
nodes.summary: Verifies that local support resources prioritize practice-provided entries, localize requested content, and preserve unverified community labels.

nodes.name: deepgram-config.test.ts
nodes.summary: Checks that Spanish and English sessions use matching Flux language hints, native Aura voices, and language-specific prompts.

nodes.name: deepgram-prompt.test.ts
nodes.summary: Validates the six safe billing concepts, exact five-tool prerequisite set, deterministic narration rules, and fixed voice-session language policy.

nodes.name: deepgram-tools.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the closed five-tool bridge, signed-session forwarding, argument rejection before network access, and confirmation-only follow-up payloads.

nodes.name: historical-narration.test.ts
nodes.summary: Proves historical narration includes source and temporal limits, suppresses all financial numbers when reconciliation fails, and never recalculates tool-returned values.

nodes.name: text-fallback.test.ts
nodes.summary: Exercises bilingual disconnected routing for bill and current-benefit requests, interruption, hardship, confirmation-gated follow-up, end-of-session clarity, and mixed-language summaries.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Creates a rate-limited synthetic BeneBot session for the fixed demo invoice, resolving Medplum seed identifiers when available and failing closed for configured-but-broken Medplum access.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Validates the fixed invoice request, resolves the signed session scope, mints a short-lived token, and returns only the synthetic patient and invoice bootstrap data.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Issues a five-minute Deepgram temporary access token to an authenticated, rate-limited BeneBot session while keeping the long-lived Deepgram API key server-only.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Authenticates the BeneBot request, enforces a per-session voice-token limit, obtains a temporary Deepgram grant, and returns a sanitized fallback-friendly error on failure.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Refreshes current benefits through the guarded Stedi test provider, optionally persists the successful snapshot to Medplum, and returns a deterministic bilingual spoken summary distinct from historical claim data.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Authenticates the session, performs the fixed synthetic current-benefits check, records persistence warnings separately, and uses a visibly labeled fixture only when explicitly allowed.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Creates a Medplum billing-review Task only after explicit patient confirmation, strict input validation, session-scope verification, and server confirmation of the persisted resource ID.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Rejects unconfirmed requests, validates a bounded billing issue summary and contact preference, then creates a scoped Medplum follow-up Task and reports its confirmed ID.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Persists a bounded conversation summary as a Medplum Communication, keeping language, answered questions, resources, follow-up, and unresolved issues structured without storing a transcript.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Authenticates and validates the summary payload, creates the scoped Communication, and returns success only after Medplum provides a resource ID.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Searches the local support-resource provider using only generic need and language filters so patient and claim data never leave BeneBot through resource discovery.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Verifies the session, validates a generic resource need and English/Spanish language, and returns up to three local support resources.

nodes.name: env.ts
nodes.summary: Defines and validates server-only BeneBot configuration, constraining Stedi to its fixed test identifiers and exposing typed guards for Medplum, Deepgram, and Stedi credentials.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Zod defaults, literals, coercion, and inferred intersection return types to keep environment validation explicit and typed.

nodes.name: getEnv
nodes.summary: Parses the process environment once and returns the cached typed BeneBot configuration.

nodes.name: requireMedplumEnv
nodes.summary: Requires both Medplum client credentials and narrows the returned environment type for authenticated server use.

nodes.name: requireDeepgramEnv
nodes.summary: Requires the server-side Deepgram API key and narrows the environment type before voice integration code uses it.

nodes.name: requireStediEnv
nodes.summary: Requires the Stedi test API key and returns a narrowed environment type for eligibility requests.

nodes.name: errors.ts
nodes.summary: Centralizes typed BeneBot errors and sanitized HTTP responses, preserving intentional user-safe messages while logging unexpected failures only with an opaque request ID and error class.

nodes.name: BeneBotError
nodes.summary: Carries a stable public error code, safe message, and HTTP status for expected BeneBot failures.

nodes.name: safeErrorResponse
nodes.summary: Converts expected errors directly and unexpected errors into sanitized JSON with an opaque diagnostic request ID.

nodes.name: server.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the server-only Medplum client boundary, credential-state detection, client-credentials login, and a retry-safe cached client promise.

nodes.name: MedplumNotConfiguredError
nodes.summary: Represents the explicit absence of Medplum client credentials so API routes can fail with a precise safe response.

nodes.name: isMedplumConfigured
nodes.summary: Reports whether both Medplum client credentials are present without initiating a network connection.

nodes.name: connectMedplum
nodes.summary: Creates a Medplum client and performs server-side client-credentials login, translating missing configuration to a domain error.

nodes.name: getMedplumClient
nodes.summary: Returns a shared asynchronous Medplum client and clears the cached promise after failed connection attempts so later calls may retry.

nodes.name: write-artifacts.ts
nodes.summary: Validates every FHIR reference against the signed session before idempotently creating Medplum Task, Communication, CoverageEligibilityRequest, and CoverageEligibilityResponse workflow artifacts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses typed FHIR R4 resources and stable identifiers so writes are scoped, reference-safe, and idempotent.

nodes.name: validateSessionReferences
nodes.summary: Reads the signed session's patient, bill, coverage, encounter, EOB, provider, and payer resources and rejects any broken cross-resource binding before a write.

nodes.name: createFollowupTask
nodes.summary: Creates an idempotent requested FHIR Task containing only the confirmed issue summary, contact preference, and signed bill context, then requires a returned ID.

nodes.name: buildSummary
nodes.summary: Builds a bounded summary that explicitly labels the historical EOB date separately from the latest eligibility status and records no full transcript.

nodes.name: createConversationCommunication
nodes.summary: Validates session and optional follow-up Task scope, then idempotently persists a completed FHIR Communication linking the bill, EOB, encounter, and confirmed Task.

nodes.name: eligibilityItems
nodes.summary: Deterministically maps only known deductible, out-of-pocket, copay, and coinsurance values into FHIR eligibility insurance items.

nodes.name: persistEligibilityResult
nodes.summary: Skips fixture data and idempotently records live eligibility request and response resources tied to the signed patient, coverage, provider, and payer context.

nodes.name: session.ts
nodes.summary: Implements signed, short-lived BeneBot JWT sessions bound to one synthetic patient, invoice, EOB, coverage, encounter, provider, and payer, plus bearer parsing and in-memory demo rate limiting.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses JOSE HS256 verification with fixed issuer, audience, algorithm, token type, and Zod claim validation before accepting browser requests.

nodes.name: getSessionSecret
nodes.summary: Loads the session signing secret and rejects missing or shorter-than-32-byte values before any JWT operation.

nodes.name: createBeneBotSession
nodes.summary: Validates a bounded TTL, binds the full bill scope into claims, and signs a short-lived HS256 JWT with a unique token ID.

nodes.name: verifyBeneBotSession
nodes.summary: Verifies signature, algorithm, issuer, audience, token type, expiry, and every required bill-scope claim before returning a session.

nodes.name: getBearerToken
nodes.summary: Extracts exactly one bearer token from the Authorization header and raises a safe authentication error otherwise.

nodes.name: verifyRequestSession
nodes.summary: Combines bearer extraction with full BeneBot JWT verification for server route handlers.

nodes.name: enforceDemoRateLimit
nodes.summary: Applies a bounded in-memory fixed-window request limit and emits a safe retry-later error when the demo limit is exceeded.

nodes.name: eligibility.ts
nodes.summary: Guards the fixed Jane Doe Stedi test request, normalizes only unambiguous payer fields, performs the sole permitted deductible derivation in deterministic code, and produces timestamped English/Spanish spoken summaries.
nodes.languageNotes: Zod passthrough schemas preserve tolerance for payer payload additions while explicit extraction leaves omitted or ambiguous benefit values unknown.

nodes.name: spokenSource
nodes.summary: Produces an English or Spanish source label that clearly distinguishes live Stedi, Medplum-bot test, and non-live fixture data.

nodes.name: spokenCheckedAt
nodes.summary: Formats an eligibility snapshot timestamp in English or Spanish with an explicit UTC time zone.

nodes.name: spokenMoney
nodes.summary: Formats a known USD amount for English or Spanish speech while rendering omitted values as not returned.

nodes.name: buildCurrentBenefitsSpokenSummary
nodes.summary: Builds deterministic English and Spanish voice text that timestamps current eligibility and explicitly states it cannot explain, validate, or replace the historical claim.

nodes.name: deriveDeductibleSummary
nodes.summary: Subtracts remaining from annual deductible only when both nonnegative values share the exact benefit level, network, and service scope; otherwise it preserves known inputs without derivation.

nodes.name: scopedAmount
nodes.summary: Converts an individual benefit amount into a normalized value paired with explicit network and service-type scope.

nodes.name: exactScopedAmount
nodes.summary: Selects exactly one individual in-network service-type-30 annual or remaining benefit, returning unknown when payer scope is ambiguous.

nodes.name: assertStediTestIdentity
nodes.summary: Fails before networking unless the entire request exactly matches the fixed synthetic Jane Doe identity and documented Stedi test literals.

nodes.name: normalizeStediResponse
nodes.summary: Parses a Stedi response and emits only clearly supported coverage, deductible, out-of-pocket, copay, and coinsurance fields with warnings for missing or ambiguous scope.

nodes.name: loadFixtureFallback
nodes.summary: Returns the captured normalized fallback fixture whose source and warnings visibly mark it as non-live.

nodes.name: DirectStediTestProvider
nodes.summary: Implements the direct Stedi test call with preflight identity enforcement, API-key authentication, timeout cancellation, response normalization, and sanitized failures.

nodes.name: createEligibilityProvider
nodes.summary: Selects the direct test provider only when a Stedi test key is configured and rejects unsupported provider modes.

nodes.name: medplum-billing-case.test.ts
nodes.summary: Integration tests prove that billing-review Tasks contain only confirmed scoped fields, omit transcripts, and are never written when the EOB-to-encounter relationship violates the signed session.

nodes.name: scopedResources
nodes.summary: Builds the minimal linked FHIR resource fixture used to exercise session-bound Medplum write validation.

nodes.name: stedi-eligibility.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the fixed-identity pre-network guard, literal Stedi request, conservative benefit normalization, scope-safe deductible derivation, bilingual historical/current disclaimer, and visibly non-live fixture fallback.

nodes.name: session.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests cover valid bill-scoped sessions and reject tampered, expired, wrong-audience, or incomplete JWTs.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Renders the Spanish staff proof view and loads server-confirmed Medplum eligibility, Task, and Communication artifacts while failing closed to clearly labeled seeded records.
nodes.languageNotes: An async Next.js server component keeps Medplum access out of the browser and uses explicit fallback copy when live records cannot be confirmed.

nodes.name: loadWorkflowArtifacts
nodes.summary: Reads patient-scoped eligibility, follow-up tasks, and conversation summaries from Medplum, correlates their FHIR references, and returns conservative fallback states when configuration or reads fail.

nodes.name: StaffPage
nodes.summary: Builds the staff-facing audit page showing a synthetic session summary and the timeline of historical, eligibility, and follow-up FHIR artifacts.

nodes.name: artifact-timeline.tsx
nodes.summary: Defines the typed workflow-artifact view model and renders an accessible chronological list of EOB, invoice, eligibility, Task, and Communication records.

nodes.name: ArtifactTimeline
nodes.summary: Renders typed workflow artifacts with status-aware identifiers, timestamps, sources, and human-readable details.

nodes.name: math.ts
nodes.summary: Implements deterministic medical-bill reconciliation for allowed charges, patient responsibility, and insurer payment using a one-cent tolerance and fail-closed validation.
nodes.languageNotes: Financial arithmetic is isolated in a pure TypeScript function so the AI layer never calculates claim amounts.

nodes.name: reconcileBillMath
nodes.summary: Checks all bill amounts for finite nonnegative values and verifies the three required billing equations within a $0.01 tolerance.

nodes.name: normalize-eob.ts
nodes.summary: Normalizes FHIR ExplanationOfBenefit adjudication into a deterministic billing structure, preserves missing values as errors outside the controlled fixture, and refuses numerical explanation when reconciliation fails.
nodes.languageNotes: FHIR and CARIN adjudication codings are mapped through a closed constant table before deterministic reconciliation.

nodes.name: BillNormalizationError
nodes.summary: Carries one or more fail-closed normalization warnings when historical adjudication data cannot support a trustworthy numerical explanation.

nodes.name: getCategory
nodes.summary: Maps supported FHIR or CARIN adjudication category codings to BeneBot's normalized amount keys while ignoring unknown systems and codes.

nodes.name: collectAmounts
nodes.summary: Collects unique normalized amounts from adjudication entries and records duplicate categories rather than silently overwriting them.

nodes.name: normalizeEob
nodes.summary: Extracts required historical adjudication amounts and service metadata, applies narrowly controlled fixture defaults, and returns reconciliation confidence plus warnings.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the normalized bill, patient, provider, payer, service, invoice, adjudication, and reconciliation contracts consumed across the deterministic billing pipeline.

nodes.name: constants.ts
nodes.summary: Centralizes BeneBot FHIR identifier systems and stable synthetic demo identifiers for idempotent Medplum lookups and writes.

nodes.name: demo-fixture.ts
nodes.summary: Validates the synthetic FHIR transaction Bundle and provides type-safe accessors for its Patient, Organization, Coverage, Encounter, EOB, and Invoice resources.

nodes.name: parseFixture
nodes.summary: Validates that the imported fixture is a FHIR transaction Bundle whose every entry contains a resource.

nodes.name: getFixtureResource
nodes.summary: Returns the first synthetic fixture resource of a requested FHIR type and throws when the fixture lacks it.

nodes.name: getFixtureResources
nodes.summary: Filters the synthetic Bundle into a type-safe list of resources matching a requested FHIR resource type.

nodes.name: queries.ts
nodes.summary: Builds patient-scoped normalized bill contexts from Medplum or the labeled local fixture, validates all FHIR reference relationships, and resolves seeded resources through stable identifiers.
nodes.languageNotes: The server-only module uses parallel FHIR reads but performs deterministic cross-resource reference checks before returning any bill context.

nodes.name: identifierValue
nodes.summary: Extracts a required stable identifier from a FHIR resource for a specific system and rejects missing identifiers.

nodes.name: buildNormalizedBillContext
nodes.summary: Validates patient, provider, payer, coverage, encounter, EOB, and invoice reference integrity before assembling a minimal bilingual-ready bill context with deterministic adjudication confidence.

nodes.name: getBillContextForSession
nodes.summary: Reads all resources bound to a signed bill session from Medplum in parallel and normalizes them only after determining whether they match the controlled demo claim.

nodes.name: getFixtureBillContext
nodes.summary: Clones synthetic FHIR resources into a requested session scope, rewires their references, builds the normalized context, and marks it as a Medplum fallback.

nodes.name: findUniqueByIdentifier
nodes.summary: Searches Medplum by a stable identifier and rejects both absent and duplicate resources before returning the confirmed ID.

nodes.name: resolveDemoSeedIds
nodes.summary: Resolves the seven canonical demo resource IDs concurrently through stable BeneBot identifier systems.

nodes.name: isMissingMedplum
nodes.summary: Provides a type guard for the explicit Medplum-not-configured failure used to select safe fixture behavior.

nodes.name: seed-medplum.ts
nodes.summary: Validates the canonical synthetic billing Bundle, seeds its FHIR resources into Medplum idempotently by stable identifier, resolves dependent references, and confirms every server write.
nodes.languageNotes: The script validates each resource server-side before create-or-update and searches again after writes to prove the persisted identity.

nodes.name: searchUnique
nodes.summary: Queries Medplum by the resource's stable BeneBot identifier and fails when duplicate matches make idempotent seeding unsafe.

nodes.name: validateOnServer
nodes.summary: Runs Medplum's FHIR validation and converts error or fatal issues into a blocking seed failure.

nodes.name: seedResource
nodes.summary: Validates, creates or updates, and then uniquely re-reads a FHIR resource so seed success is never claimed before server confirmation.

nodes.name: resolveFixtureReferences
nodes.summary: Replaces fixture URNs with confirmed Medplum references and revalidates that serialization preserved the expected FHIR resource type.

nodes.name: assertCanonicalDemo
nodes.summary: Guards the P0 fixture invariants: complete FHIR billing resources, reconciled $620 responsibility, fixed Stedi member, Spanish preference, and linked encounter references.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Authenticates the server-side Medplum client, seeds resources in dependency order, records resolved references, and prints only the resulting demo IDs and identifier systems.

nodes.name: fixture-bill-context.test.ts
nodes.summary: Integration test proving that the local fixture produces a session-scoped, reconciled $620 context with Spanish preference, minimal patient data, and an explicit Medplum fallback warning.

nodes.name: billing-math.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests the deterministic billing equations, one-cent tolerance, discrepancy behavior, and rejection of invalid financial amounts.

nodes.name: eob-normalizer.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests deterministic EOB extraction, duplicate-category detection, required member liability, USD enforcement, and fixture-only zero defaults without exposing diagnosis data.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Renders the Spanish-first synthetic patient bill page for the fixed BeneBot invoice, including secure-context messaging, a reconciled historical claim breakdown, and the conversation launcher. It explicitly separates the historical EOB from any current benefits lookup.
nodes.languageNotes: An async Next.js App Router page awaits dynamic route parameters and uses semantic, localized JSX with explicit accessibility labels.

nodes.name: BillPage
nodes.summary: Validates the demo invoice identifier and composes the patient-facing statement, historical claim breakdown, bilingual conversation experience, and source-distinction notice.

nodes.name: bill-breakdown.tsx
nodes.summary: Presents the deterministic Spanish-language arithmetic for Jane Doe's historical synthetic claim, including billed, discounted, allowed, insurer-paid, and patient-responsibility amounts. Source and date labels prevent the historical deductible from being mistaken for current eligibility.

nodes.name: BillBreakdown
nodes.summary: Renders the fixed, reconciled historical EOB line items as an accessible definition list with an emphasized $620 patient responsibility.

nodes.name: bill-experience.tsx
nodes.summary: Implements the client-side transition from the bill into a secure BeneBot conversation by requesting a server-created session token and rendering the voice/text panel only after validation. It provides loading and Spanish error states while advertising English support and avoiding repeated identity collection.
nodes.languageNotes: The component keeps the untyped network response as unknown and narrows it with a dedicated TypeScript type guard before storing the session token.

nodes.name: BillExperience
nodes.summary: Creates a session through the BeneBot server route, validates the response, manages launch and error state, and swaps the launcher for the bilingual voice/text assistant panel.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Defines the repository-wide engineering contract for BeneBot, including its synthetic-only scope, historical-versus-current evidence boundary, server-side integrations, deterministic billing math, security rules, and validation gates.

nodes.name: BENEBOT_BUILD_SPEC.md
nodes.summary: Canonical end-to-end specification for BeneBot's Jane Doe demo, covering architecture, FHIR resources, deterministic bill normalization, signed sessions, Deepgram voice, Stedi eligibility, resource search, Medplum writes, UI contracts, testing, and phased delivery.
nodes.languageNotes: The Markdown specification combines normative requirements, TypeScript and JSON contract examples, route definitions, trust boundaries, and a complete implementation sequence.

nodes.name: BENEBOT_RESEARCH_AGENT_PROMPTS.md
nodes.summary: Defines six bounded research lanes and a final independent adjudication prompt for producing BeneBot's authoritative bilingual concept, misconception, utterance, rubric, and tool-prerequisite packet.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Redirects Claude-compatible agents to the canonical repository instructions in AGENTS.md so all coding assistants share the same safety and delivery constraints.

nodes.name: CODEX_START_PROMPT.md
nodes.summary: Provides a copy-ready kickoff prompt that tells Codex to ground itself in the build specification, execute one phase at a time, preserve strict evidence boundaries, and run each required validation gate.

nodes.name: CONVERSATION_RELIABILITY_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Plans the bounded reliability layer for BeneBot conversations: eight phase-aware rubrics, closed-tool prerequisites, deterministic enforcement, an adjudicated bilingual concept library, evidence-linked transcript evaluation, and staged integration.

nodes.name: IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md
nodes.summary: Translates the build specification into a time-boxed Spanish-first hackathon execution plan with fixed technical choices, staged work waves, validation checkpoints, demo choreography, and an explicit fallback-and-cut ladder.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Operational runbook for installing, configuring, seeding, testing, and rehearsing BeneBot, with explicit setup instructions for Medplum, Deepgram, and Stedi plus honest degraded-mode behavior and the Spanish-first demo script.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Defines the private Next.js application package, its development, type-check, Vitest, Playwright, build, and Medplum seed scripts, and runtime dependencies for Deepgram UI, Medplum FHIR, JWT handling, and Zod validation.

nodes.name: spanish-concept-library.json
nodes.summary: Stores six es-419 medical-billing concepts with preferred and alternative terminology, patient-facing explanations, confusion repairs, bounded analogies, comprehension checks, utterance variants, forbidden claims, and pronunciation guidance.
nodes.languageNotes: The JSON models neutral Latin American Spanish as structured runtime guidance rather than direct English translation, with explicit false-claim and TTS safeguards.

nodes.name: spanish-review-notes.md
nodes.summary: Records the linguistic review rationale behind the Spanish concept library, including U.S. Latino regional choices, billing-term distinctions, false friends, remaining ambiguities, and pronunciation guidance for voice output.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: Configures strict TypeScript checking for the Next.js application with ESNext modules, React JSX, incremental compilation, the @ path alias, and generated Next.js type inputs.
nodes.languageNotes: Strict mode and noEmit make TypeScript a validation gate while Next.js retains control of bundling and emitted artifacts.

nodes.name: INTEGRATION_NOTES.md
nodes.summary: Records how the approved research packet was incorporated into the bounded Jane Doe P0 while keeping patient-specific values out of prompts. It also resolves conflicts between research rubrics, unsupported tool prerequisites, runtime authority, and evaluation-only material.

nodes.name: adjudication-report.md
nodes.summary: Documents the final adjudication of six BeneBot research packets, including the accepted six-concept P0 vocabulary, repaired bilingual analogies, evaluation-only content, and rejected unsafe material. The report recommends the reconciled packet for bounded P0 incorporation.

nodes.name: canonical-concepts.json
nodes.summary: Defines the canonical English and Spanish health-literacy library for six P0 billing concepts. Each entry combines preferred terminology, definitions, utterance variants, comprehension checks, Spanish pronunciation guidance, and shared factual boundaries.
nodes.languageNotes: The JSON uses parallel English and Spanish structures so evaluators can compare meaning while preserving language-specific terminology and pronunciation guidance.

nodes.name: eight-rubric-spec.json
nodes.summary: Defines eight prioritized research evaluation dimensions covering financial non-invention, historical/current separation, prerequisite tool ordering, confirmed external outcomes, bilingual equivalence, natural language, safe analogies, and conversational warmth.

nodes.name: runtime-concepts.json
nodes.summary: Provides runtime-oriented English and Spanish explanation patterns for the six P0 billing concepts, including first explanations, confusion repairs, forbidden phrases, optional analogies, and explicit analogy boundaries. Integration notes constrain patient-specific values in this research artifact from entering live prompt guidance.
nodes.languageNotes: Each concept has parallel language-scoped response fields, enabling semantic alignment without requiring literal translation.

nodes.name: source-ledger.md
nodes.summary: Traces the packet's factual boundaries, English and Spanish concept content, analogy decisions, and synthetic bilingual evaluation cases back to five upstream research sources. A coverage matrix exposes source gaps and normalized concept identifiers for the six-concept P0 set.

nodes.name: tool-prerequisite-matrix.json
nodes.summary: Maps patient-specific claims about the six P0 billing concepts to the research packet's proposed prerequisite tools. The integration notes treat this matrix as evaluation provenance because several named tools and requested facts are unsupported by the closed BeneBot runtime tool set.

nodes.name: benebot-fhir-seed.json
nodes.summary: Defines the synthetic FHIR R4 transaction bundle for BeneBot's Jane Doe billing scenario, linking the patient, provider, payer, coverage, encounter, ExplanationOfBenefit, and invoice. Its adjudication totals encode the canonical reconciled $620 patient-responsibility example used by the demo and tests.
nodes.languageNotes: The JSON models a FHIR transaction Bundle with urn:uuid references so dependent resources can be resolved before idempotent Medplum writes.

nodes.name: demo-resources.json
nodes.summary: Catalogs five bilingual synthetic support resources for payment plans, billing review, payer contact, advocacy, and financial assistance. Each record carries provenance, verification status, fictional-data disclosure, contact hours, and prioritized English and Spanish instructions.
nodes.languageNotes: Each resource stores parallel en/es summaries and instruction arrays while keeping verification and disclosure metadata language-independent.

nodes.name: stedi-aetna-test-request.json
nodes.summary: Captures the sole synthetic Aetna eligibility request permitted for BeneBot's Stedi test integration. It fixes the trading partner, provider NPI, Jane Doe subscriber identity, and service type 30 so deviations can fail before a network call.

nodes.name: stedi-normalized-fallback.json
nodes.summary: Provides a visibly labeled normalized fallback for current-benefits retrieval when live Stedi test data is unavailable. It preserves a separate check timestamp, deductible and out-of-pocket scopes, sample copay and coinsurance details, and warnings that the fallback does not explain historical claim adjudication.

nodes.name: .understandignore
nodes.summary: Defines the opt-in exclusion patterns available to the Understand Anything scanner, including generated output, credentials, test suites, fixtures, and language-specific test conventions. All suggested patterns remain commented so the current graph includes the full project surface.

nodes.name: config.json
nodes.summary: Stores project-level Understand Anything preferences, currently selecting English for generated knowledge-graph text.

nodes.name: globals.css
nodes.summary: Defines BeneBot's shared visual system and responsive layouts for the Spanish-first landing page, patient billing experience, conversation panel, and staff workflow timeline. It includes accessibility-aware reduced-motion behavior and semantic state styling for historical and current sources.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses modern CSS features including OKLCH colors, custom properties, responsive clamp sizing, and a reduced-motion media query.

nodes.name: layout.tsx
nodes.summary: Provides the Next.js root layout, bilingual demo metadata, Geist font variables, and a Spanish document-language default for every BeneBot page.

nodes.name: RootLayout
nodes.summary: Wraps all application routes in the Spanish-language HTML shell and applies shared font variables and full-height layout classes.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Renders BeneBot's Spanish-first synthetic billing-email landing page and routes Jane Doe into the fixed demonstration invoice while clearly disclosing the synthetic-data context.

nodes.name: Home
nodes.summary: Builds the accessible email-preview entry experience for invoice BENEBOT-INV-1001, including synthetic-data disclosure and English availability messaging.

nodes.name: rejected-content.jsonl
nodes.summary: Records 11 healthcare-billing content candidates that were deliberately excluded from the trusted evaluation or response corpus, together with source provenance and rejection reasons.

nodes.name: transcript-eval-cases.jsonl
nodes.summary: Defines 24 balanced English and Spanish synthetic conversation cases covering billing concepts, interruptions, corrections, frustration, scoped refusals, historical-versus-current distinctions, and human follow-up.

nodes.name: demo-resources.json
nodes.summary: Provides five bilingual synthetic support-resource records used by the fallback search provider, preserving practice, fictional, and community-reported provenance along with explicit verification disclosures and priority ordering.

nodes.name: eslint.config.mjs
nodes.summary: Composes the Next.js Core Web Vitals and TypeScript lint presets while explicitly excluding framework and build outputs from static analysis.

nodes.name: conversation-evaluation.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the evaluation-only reliability contract for BeneBot conversations: eight executable rubrics, strict bilingual gold-case schemas, tool-disposition checks, packet loading, and evidence-linked run records. It keeps research rubric conflicts visible without promoting them into runtime criteria and validates that every score cites an observed turn or tool event.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Zod superRefine checks for cross-field invariants such as rubric uniqueness, required versus forbidden tool separation, hard-failure consistency, and referential integrity of evaluation evidence.

nodes.name: findResearchRubricConflicts
nodes.summary: Compares the research packet's eight rubric definitions with BeneBot's approved executable rubric set and returns every semantic or priority mismatch for explicit adjudication.

nodes.name: classifyPacketToolName
nodes.summary: Deterministically classifies a tool referenced by the research packet as runtime-supported, deliberately deferred, or unsupported.

nodes.name: collectPacketToolReferences
nodes.summary: Collects every unique tool named by evaluation cases and prerequisite rules, sorts them stably, and annotates each with its supported, deferred, or unsupported disposition.

nodes.name: readJsonLines
nodes.summary: Reads non-empty JSONL records from disk and converts malformed records into location-specific errors that identify the exact file and line.

nodes.name: loadGoldPacket
nodes.summary: Loads and strictly validates the research rubric, transcript cases, and tool-prerequisite matrix, rejecting duplicate case identifiers and returning both rubric conflicts and normalized tool references.

nodes.name: next.config.ts
nodes.summary: Configures Next.js Turbopack to treat the BeneBot repository as its explicit compilation root.

nodes.name: playwright.config.ts
nodes.summary: Configures browser rehearsals under tests/e2e against a locally managed Next.js development server on port 3000, reusing an existing instance when available.

nodes.name: postcss.config.mjs
nodes.summary: Enables Tailwind CSS processing through the PostCSS plugin used by the application stylesheet pipeline.

nodes.name: text-happy-path.spec.ts
nodes.summary: Rehearses Jane Doe's complete Spanish-first text fallback: synthetic email entry, secure bill context, historical and current benefit separation, interruption handling, confirmed follow-up persistence, and staff-facing FHIR artifacts.

nodes.name: server-only.ts
nodes.summary: Provides the empty Vitest alias target for the server-only package so server modules can be exercised in the Node test environment without client-boundary runtime behavior.

nodes.name: conversation-evaluation.test.ts
nodes.summary: Verifies the evaluation reliability contract: exact executable rubric IDs, strict parsing of 24 unique synthetic cases, explicit handling of deferred and unsupported tools, and evidence-linked run records without raw audio.

nodes.name: vitest.config.mts
nodes.summary: Configures Vitest's Node environment, repository-root path alias, server-only test shim, and unit-test discovery convention.

layers.name: Patient and Staff Experience
layers.description: Next.js pages, shared styling, and accessible React components present the synthetic bill, bilingual voice and text conversation, deterministic arithmetic, and staff-visible workflow timeline.

layers.name: Authenticated Server API
layers.description: Next.js route handlers enforce the signed BeneBot session boundary while exposing the closed bill, benefits, resources, follow-up, summary, and temporary Deepgram-token operations.

layers.name: Deterministic Billing and Trust Core
layers.description: Pure billing normalization and reconciliation, shared contracts, scoped JWT sessions, and sanitized errors keep financial explanations deterministic and patient access fail-closed.

layers.name: Bilingual Voice and Conversation Policy
layers.description: Deepgram configuration, the English/Spanish billing dictionary, tool prerequisites, deterministic fallback routing, and the closed tool bridge govern every spoken or typed conversation.

layers.name: Healthcare Integrations and FHIR Workflow
layers.description: Server-only adapters validate configuration, read and write scoped Medplum FHIR R4 resources, refresh timestamped Stedi eligibility, and search disclosure-preserving support resources.

layers.name: Synthetic Demo and Evaluation Evidence
layers.description: FHIR fixtures, guarded Stedi inputs, bilingual resource catalogs, adjudicated concept packets, and transcript cases provide the safe synthetic evidence used by the demo and its reliability checks.

layers.name: Verification and Conversation Evaluation
layers.description: Executable rubrics plus unit, integration, and browser tests prove the reconciled bill math, security boundaries, bilingual behavior, external-workflow confirmation, and full Jane Doe happy path.

layers.name: Product, Safety, and Delivery Documentation
layers.description: The canonical specification, repository policies, research prompts, reliability plan, runbook, and execution guides preserve BeneBot's synthetic-only scope and historical-versus-current evidence boundary.

layers.name: Build, Test, Analysis, and Seed Tooling
layers.description: Strict TypeScript, Next.js, Tailwind, Vitest, Playwright, lint, knowledge-graph, package, and idempotent Medplum seed controls make the demo reproducible and inspectable.

tour.title: BeneBot at a Glance
tour.description: Start with the operational README to understand BeneBot as a synthetic-data guide for one Jane Doe medical bill, not a general health-record assistant. It introduces the Spanish-first demo, the historical-versus-current evidence boundary, and the honest degraded modes that keep the experience useful when an external service is unavailable.

tour.title: Enter the Demo
tour.description: The root layout establishes a bilingual, Spanish-default application shell, while the landing page presents a clearly synthetic billing email and routes Jane Doe into the fixed invoice. Together they show how the demo begins with disclosure and a bounded scenario before any patient-specific server work occurs.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router layouts establish shared document metadata and presentation, while page modules define route-specific server-rendered entry points.

tour.title: Read the Bill
tour.description: The invoice page and bill components turn the opening scenario into a secure patient journey: first show the reconciled historical claim, then create a server-issued session before revealing the assistant. Source dates and labels are part of the product logic, preventing historical deductible amounts from being mistaken for today's remaining benefits.
tour.languageLesson: The server page owns trusted data loading, while the client experience owns the interactive transition into a signed conversation; this split keeps secrets and patient scope out of the browser bundle.

tour.title: Deterministic Money Boundary
tour.description: BeneBot does not ask an LLM to calculate a bill. The billing types, EOB normalizer, and reconciliation functions produce a single deterministic structure, enforce the allowed-charge and responsibility equations within one cent, and suppress numerical narration when the source data does not reconcile.
tour.languageLesson: Pure TypeScript functions and explicit result contracts make financial transformations independently testable. The LLM receives already-normalized values and wording constraints, not arithmetic authority.

tour.title: Signed Trust Envelope
tour.description: Building on the deterministic bill, BeneBot binds each short-lived JWT to one patient, invoice, EOB, coverage, encounter, provider, and payer. Shared contracts define the closed tool surface, while sanitized errors and server-only environment validation make every API route fail closed instead of trusting identifiers supplied later by the browser.
tour.languageLesson: Zod-validated boundary objects and narrow TypeScript contracts turn untrusted request data into explicit, typed capabilities. A signed session is treated as a scope envelope, not merely a login flag.

tour.title: Bilingual Concept Policy
tour.description: The assistant's English and Spanish explanations come from a code-owned healthcare-billing dictionary and an adjudicated es-419 concept library, not improvised definitions. Prompt rules and per-tool prerequisites attach safe analogies, forbidden claims, fixed-language behavior, and server-confirmed evidence requirements to each concept before the voice model can narrate it.
tour.languageLesson: Separating canonical domain language from model prompts makes bilingual behavior reviewable and versionable. The prompt orchestrates policy, while structured dictionaries remain the source of explanatory meaning.

tour.title: Voice with Text Parity
tour.description: The main conversation panel connects Deepgram's bilingual Agent experience to exactly five BeneBot tools and presents every call as running, confirmed, or failed. Deepgram uses a temporary server-issued token, matching Flux recognition and Aura voices for English or Spanish, while the deterministic text router preserves the same safe journey whenever voice is unavailable.
tour.languageLesson: A React client may manage microphone state and render transcripts, but credentials and healthcare integrations stay behind authenticated routes. Tool schemas form a constrained bridge between probabilistic conversation and deterministic server actions.

tour.title: Explain Historical Adjudication
tour.description: The bill-context route is the historical evidence tool: it loads only the session-scoped EOB and invoice context, permits a visibly identified fixture fallback, and rejects unreconciled numbers. Its bilingual narration then states both the source and the temporal limitation, so the assistant never presents old adjudication as proof of current coverage.

tour.title: Refresh Current Benefits
tour.description: Current eligibility takes a separate route through the guarded Stedi test integration and receives its own check timestamp. The fixed Jane Doe request must match before any network call, ambiguous payer fields remain unknown, and a fallback is explicitly labeled as non-live rather than allowed to validate the historical claim.

tour.title: Persist Confirmed Follow-Up
tour.description: Medplum is both the source for scoped FHIR R4 billing context and the destination for confirmed workflow artifacts. The server adapter validates references before idempotently writing a billing-review Task or bounded Communication; the routes report success only after Medplum returns the persisted resource identifiers, and no full transcript is stored.
tour.languageLesson: FHIR references are integrity constraints between resources, so dependent writes must validate the session-bound Patient, Encounter, EOB, and Coverage relationships before creating Task or Communication records.

tour.title: Prove the Workflow
tour.description: The staff page closes the loop by loading the server-confirmed eligibility, Task, and Communication artifacts into an accessible timeline beside the original EOB and invoice. This is the demo's operational proof: the patient-facing promise becomes a visible FHIR workflow, while seeded records remain clearly labeled when live Medplum is unavailable.

tour.title: Safe Synthetic World
tour.description: The fixed FHIR transaction bundle supplies the linked Jane Doe patient, payer, coverage, encounter, EOB, and invoice behind the whole tour, and the idempotent seed script can reproduce it in Medplum. Separate bilingual resource fixtures support hardship and billing-help searches without sending patient data to a search provider, while preserving fictional and community-reported disclosures.
tour.languageLesson: Stable synthetic identifiers make repeated FHIR seeding idempotent and keep integration tests reproducible. Provenance fields travel with resource-search results so the UI cannot accidentally erase their disclosure status.

tour.title: Evaluation Evidence Packet
tour.description: BeneBot's conversation quality is grounded in an adjudicated packet rather than a vague notion of helpfulness. Canonical concepts, eight safety rubrics, 24 bilingual transcript cases, and an evidence-linked evaluation contract test historical/current separation, financial non-invention, tool ordering, confirmation, natural language, and safe analogies without promoting rejected material into runtime policy.

tour.title: Verify Every Boundary
tour.description: Focused unit and integration tests prove the architecture's hardest claims: exact one-cent bill reconciliation, safe bilingual prompting, tamper-resistant sessions, conservative Stedi normalization, and scoped Medplum writes. These tests turn the earlier design rules into executable gates and demonstrate that failed prerequisites prevent narration or persistence rather than producing plausible-looking success.

tour.title: Rehearse the Whole Story
tour.description: Finish with the browser test that rehearses the complete Spanish-first text path from synthetic email through bill explanation, current-benefit separation, interruption, confirmed follow-up, and staff-visible FHIR artifacts. The canonical build specification and package scripts show how that happy path is governed and how type-check, unit, build, and end-to-end checks turn the hackathon demo into a reproducible system.
tour.languageLesson: Playwright tests behavior across real route and UI boundaries, while Vitest covers pure logic and server modules. Together they validate both the deterministic core and the user's end-to-end experience.
